ACT, 1961, PENDING BEFORE THE HONBLE XXIV ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE AT BANGALORE.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The petitioner/accused No.1 is sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, accused No.1/husband had subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demand was made to bring money from the parental home.
NC: 2023:KHC:33884 3.

The parties are present before this Court and have filed a joint affidavit stating that the accused had filed a petition for dissolving the marriage with defacto complainant and the said petition was allowed dissolving the marriage.

The defacto complainant had filed Crl.Misc.No.54/2022 before the V MMTC, Bengaluru under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act and in the said proceedings, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves and accused No.1 has paid a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards permanent alimony.
The second respondent/defacto complainant has no objection to quash the impugned proceedings.
4. The joint affidavit is placed on record.

sentences.text: Though the offences are cognizable and non compoundable, however having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the second respondent/defacto complainant having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioner is subjected to trial, since the probability of his conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:33884 ORDER i.
Criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.26285/2022 on the file of XXIV Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner/accused No.1 is sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The defacto complainant had filed Crl.Misc.No.54/2022 before the V MMTC, Bengaluru under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act and in the said proceedings, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves and accused No.1 has paid a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards permanent alimony.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The second respondent/defacto complainant has no objection to quash the impugned proceedings.
Though the offences are cognizable and non compoundable, however having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the second respondent/defacto complainant having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioner is subjected to trial, since the probability of his conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Criminal petition is allowed.
